chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Hanan ibn Sadir, from Hakim ibn Jubayr al-Asadi, who said:

I heard Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) saying: Indeed, Allah sends down an angel every night with him three mithqals of the musk of Paradise, and he drops them in this Euphrates of yours. And there is no river in the east of the earth nor in its west that is greater in blessing than it.

key_terms.مَثَاقِيلَ: A unit of weight, specifically three mithqals

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual significance of the Euphrates River according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (a.s.) narrates that every night an angel descends carrying three mithqals of musk from Paradise and casts them into the Euphrates River, making it the most blessed river on earth from east to west. This tradition, recorded by Ibn Qulawayh in *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, underscores the Euphrates' unique spiritual status in Shia piety, linking its physical waters to divine sustenance and serving as a focal point for ritual purity (Ghusl) and devotional visitation.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 12. Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan (ibn Aḥmad ibn Walīd) narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan Al-Saffār, from ‘Abbās ibn Ma’rūf, from ‘Ali ibn Mahziyār, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl, from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr, from Ḥakīm ibn Jubayr Al-Asadi, who said:

‘Ali ibn Ḥusain (Imam Sajjād (a.s.)) said: Every night, Allāh sends down an angel who has three particles of musk from the musk of Paradise with him and he drops them in the Euphrates River (which is close to you). There is no river more blessed than the Euphrates (River) anywhere in the earth, from the east to the west.
